- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecasted peaks by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) or volatile, model underestimates downside risk; increase forecasted lows by 5–10%.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days); apply a 1–2 day lag correction to peak forecasts.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecasted price deviates >1.5σ from 18-day moving average, adjust toward historical mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model underperforms in early period (days 1–10) when sentiment is neutral or negative — increase early forecast by 3–5% to compensate for lag.
- If sentiment turns bullish sharply (e.g., >0.8 in 2–3 days), model often fails to capture momentum — increase forecast slope by 10–15% for next 5 days.
